nindian-history-129-19.s: Which of the following took place last?
nindian-history-129-19.x: The Rampa Rebellion of 1922–24 came after the Indigo Revolt (1859–60), the Deccan Riots (1875) and the Munda Ulgulan (1899–1900).

n31f1460c64e.s: The first Factories Act, which curbed child labour, was passed in:
n31f1460c64e.x: The first Factories Act came in 1881, after the Bombay factory commission of 1875; the Act of 1891 followed.

ndb0e986fac1.s: How many labour and communist leaders were tried in the Meerut Conspiracy Case (1929)?
ndb0e986fac1.x: 31 leaders, including Dange, Muzaffar Ahmad, Usmani and Philip Spratt, were tried; the long trial made them martyrs.

n40a30342943.s: In which year was a socialist political school held at Madanapalle in Andhra?
n40a30342943.x: Madanapalle is associated with 1938; Kothapatnam was 1937 and the Kankipadu Rajakeeya Pathashala 1939.

new.s: The Bhil rising of 1818-31 took place in:
new.x: The Bhil rising of 1818-31 was in Khandesh (Maharashtra); Singhbhum, Ghumsar and Barabhum were the regions of the Ho, Khond and Bhumij risings.

new.s: Ganga Narain is associated with which tribal revolt?
new.x: Ganga Narain led the Bhumij revolt of 1832-33 in Barabhum, Manbhum; the Kol rising was led by Budhu Bhagat.

new.s: The Jaintia rising of 1860-62 was led by:
new.x: U Kiang Nangbah led the Jaintia rising against house tax and income tax; Tirot Sing led the Khasi rising of 1829-33.

new.s: U Kiang Nangbah, leader of the Jaintia rising, was hanged in December 1862 at:
new.x: U Kiang Nangbah was hanged at Jowai on 30 December 1862.

new.s: The Kuki rising of 1917-19 in Manipur was triggered by:
o: Forced recruitment into the Labour Corps for France
The imposition of house tax and income tax
new.x: The Kuki rising was set off by forced recruitment into the Labour Corps for France during the First World War.

new.s: The Santhal Hul of 1855 began at:
new.x: The Hul began at Bhognadih on 30 June 1855, observed as Hul Divas.

new.s: Approximately how many Santhals were killed when the Hul was crushed in 1856?
new.x: Over 15,000 Santhals were killed; about 30,000 had proclaimed Santhal Raj.

new.s: After the Santhal Hul, the Santhal Parganas was made a separate:
new.x: Santhal Parganas became a separate non-regulation district (Act XXXVII of 1855) with laws protecting tribal land.

new.s: Birsa Munda died on 9 June 1900 in:
new.x: Birsa Munda died in Ranchi jail on 9 June 1900.

new.s: Birsa Munda was captured on 3 February 1900 in the:
new.x: Birsa was captured in the Jamkopai forest near Chakradharpur (West Singhbhum) on 3 February 1900.

new.s: Which one of the following is NOT correct about Birsa Munda?
o: He led the Kol rising of 1831-32
new.x: The Kol rising of 1831-32 was led by Budhu Bhagat; Birsa was born only in 1875.

new.s: The Paika Bidroha of 1817 took place in present-day:
new.x: The Paika Bidroha under Bakshi Jagabandhu broke out at Khurda in Odisha, not West Bengal.

new.s: The Ramosi risings in Maharashtra followed the:
new.x: The Ramosis rose after the fall of the Peshwa, in 1822 and again in 1825-26 around Satara.

new.s: Wilkinson's Rule (1837) governed the Kolhan through:
new.x: After the Kol rising, Wilkinson's Rule of 1837 governed the Kolhan through the Munda-Manki chiefs.

new.s: Cleveland's conciliatory plan for the Paharias in the 1780s was framed when he was Collector of:
new.x: Cleveland, Collector of Bhagalpur in the 1780s, ruled the Paharias through their hill chiefs.

new.s: The Santhal Parganas Tenancy (Supplementary Provisions) Act was passed in:
new.x: The SPT Act is of 1949; 1908 is the Chotanagpur Tenancy Act and 1872 the Santhal Parganas Settlement Regulation.

new.s:
Consider the following statements about tribal land laws:
1. The Chotanagpur Tenancy Act, 1908 recognised Khuntkatti rights.
2. The Chotanagpur Tenancy Act was passed before the Ulgulan of 1899-1900.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
new.x: The CNT Act of 1908 recognised Khuntkatti rights, but it came after Birsa's Ulgulan of 1899-1900.

new.s: The Eki movement (1921-22) in Mewar was led by:
new.x: Motilal Tejawat led the Eki movement in Mewar; Govind Giri led the Lasodia movement.

new.s: Govind Giri founded the Samp Sabha among the Bhils in:
new.x: Govind Giri founded the Samp Sabha in 1883; 1913 is the year of the Mangarh massacre.

new.s: During the Rampa rising of 1879, Darabandala Chandrayya burnt which police station?
new.x: Chandrayya burnt the Addatheegala police station; Ambul Reddy attacked Vaddagudem.

new.s: The Koya rising of 1879-80 was led by:
new.x: Tomas (Tomma) Dora led the Koya rising of 1879-80.

new.s: Which of the following pairs is INCORRECTLY matched?
new.x: Komaram Bheem's Gond movement was of 1938-44; the other pairs are correct.

new.s: In tribal history, 'Khuntkatti' refers to:
o: A reform item of Birsa Munda
new.x: Khuntkatti was the joint landholding system of the Mundas, not a reform of Birsa; its destruction led to the Ulgulan.

new.s: The term 'Meriah' refers to:
new.x: Meriah was the human sacrifice of the Khonds; its ban helped cause the Khond rising.

new.s: The Girni Kamgar Union of Bombay (1928) was founded by:
new.x: The Girni Kamgar Union was founded in 1928 by S.A. Dange and the communists; B.P. Wadia founded the Madras Labour Union.

new.s: The Ahmedabad Textile Labour Association (1920) was founded by Gandhi along with:
new.x: Gandhi founded the Majoor Mahajan Sangh with Anasuya Sarabhai, its president for life.

new.s: The Indian National Trade Union Congress (INTUC) was set up by the Congress in:
new.x: INTUC was set up in 1947; AITUC dates from 1920 and the Hind Mazdoor Sabha from 1948.

new.s: Who was the Vice President of AITUC at its founding in 1920?
new.x: Joseph Baptista was Vice President; Lajpat Rai presided and Diwan Chaman Lal was General Secretary.

new.s: The Royal Commission on Labour (Whitley Commission), appointed in 1929, submitted its report in:
new.x: The Whitley Commission was appointed in 1929 and reported in 1931.

new.s: The Public Safety Bill of 1929 was aimed at:
o: Foreign communists such as Philip Spratt
new.x: The Public Safety Bill targeted foreign communists like Philip Spratt; the Trade Disputes Act banned sympathetic strikes.

new.s: The Communist Party of India was banned in Hyderabad State in:
new.x: The CPI was banned in Hyderabad State in 1946; the British all-India ban of 1934 was lifted in 1942.

new.s: The Communist Party of India (Marxist) dates its founding from:
new.x: The CPI(M) dates the party from Tashkent 1920, while the CPI dates itself from the Kanpur conference of 1925.

new.s: The Peshawar conspiracy cases (1922-27) were against:
o: Leaders of the Girni Kamgar Union
Members of the Congress Socialist Party
Organisers of the Workers and Peasants Party
Muhajirs trained in Moscow and Tashkent
new.x: The Peshawar cases tried Muhajirs who had trained in Moscow and Tashkent and were arrested on return across the North-West Frontier.

new.s: Which one of the following is NOT correct about the Congress Socialist Party?
o: Ram Manohar Lohia was its first General Secretary
Acharya Narendra Dev was its President
It was founded at Patna in 1934
Jayaprakash Narayan was its General Secretary
new.x: Lohia was a founder; Jayaprakash Narayan was the General Secretary.

new.s:
Consider the following statements about the Congress Socialist Party:
1. It was founded at Patna in May 1934.
2. Its policies were fixed at Bombay in October 1934.
3. Jawaharlal Nehru formally joined it.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
new.x: The CSP was founded at Patna in May 1934 and its policies were fixed at Bombay in October 1934; Nehru did not formally join it.

new.s: N.G. Ranga set up the Rajakeeya Pathashala at Kankipadu in:
new.x: Ranga set up the Rajakeeya Pathashala at Kankipadu in 1939.

new.s: The Workers and Peasants Party began in 1925 at Calcutta as the:
new.x: It began as the Labour Swaraj Party (Kazi Nazrul Islam, Hemanta Kumar Sarkar) and was renamed the Workers and Peasants Party of Bengal in 1926.

new.s: The Hyderabad State Comrades Association was formed in:
new.x: The Hyderabad State Comrades Association was formed in 1939, with Makhdoom Mohiuddin as a leading figure.

new.s: The journal 'The Socialist' was edited by:
new.x: S.A. Dange edited The Socialist; M.N. Roy edited Vanguard and Muzaffar Ahmad edited Navayug and Langal.

new.s: Which was the first communist paper of India?
new.x: M.N. Roy's Vanguard was the first communist paper; Kranti was a CPI Marathi weekly.

new.s: The Andhra Communist Party was formed at Kakinada in January 1936 with whom as Secretary?
new.x: P. Sundarayya was the Secretary of the Andhra Communist Party formed at Kakinada in January 1936.

new.s: The second Communist Conference in Andhra, attended by P.C. Joshi, was held in 1938 at:
new.x: The second Communist Conference was held at Vijayawada in 1938; the party itself was formed at Kakinada in 1936.

new.s: The Andhra Socialist Party was founded on 23 June 1934 at:
new.x: The Andhra unit of the CSP was founded at Vijayawada; the all-India CSP was founded at Patna.

new.s: The first session of the Andhra Socialist Party in 1935 was presided over by:
new.x: Tenneti Viswanatham presided over the first session in 1935.

new.s: The Raithu Rakshana Sangham (1934) was founded by:
new.x: N.G. Ranga founded the Raithu Rakshana Sangham in 1934, the year he also formed the Andhra Socialist Party.

new.s: Which leader left the Congress, joined the KMPP and then led the Praja Socialist Party in Andhra?
new.x: Tanguturi Prakasam joined the KMPP and then led the PSP in Andhra.

new.s: The Andhra Swaraj Party (1934) is associated with:
new.x: Gadicherla Harisarvottama Rao formed the Andhra Swaraj Party in 1934.

new.s: P. Sundarayya was the joint secretary of which youth meeting in 1935?
new.x: Sundarayya was joint secretary of the Vizag Yuva Mahasabha of 1935; the Kakinada Mahasabha was in 1936.

new.s: The 1938 political school at Hindupur was organised by:
new.x: The Hindupur school of 1938 was run by the communist Idukallu Sadasivan; Ranga ran Madanapalle that year.

new.s: The Telugu journal 'Udayini' was edited by:
new.x: Udayini was edited by Kompella Janardhana Rao, not Ranga, who edited Navayuga and Prajamitra.

new.s: Which was the first wholly socialist Telugu journal, started at Rajahmundry in 1937?
new.x: Navasakti, started at Rajahmundry on 15 December 1937, was the first wholly socialist Telugu journal.

new.s: The Congress Socialist Party expelled the communists in:
new.x: The CSP expelled the communists in 1940; the 'People's War' line of 1941 widened the break.

new.s: The Kisan Mazdoor Praja Party was formed by J.B. Kripalani in:
new.x: The KMPP was formed in 1951; it merged with the Socialist Party in 1952 to form the PSP.

new.s: Though the PSP demanded Tirupati in 1953, which place was chosen as the capital of Andhra State?
new.x: The PSP wanted Tirupati, but Kurnool was chosen as the capital.

new.s:
Consider the following statements about the 1952 Madras Assembly election:
1. The United Front chose Tanguturi Prakasam as its leader.
2. Governor Sri Prakasa invited Prakasam to form the government.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
new.x: The United Front chose Prakasam, but Governor Sri Prakasa invited Rajaji instead.
